regions.label: Idea
regions.intent: Pin down what you're building, for whom, and why now. The questions below shape every other region.

questions.prompt: Can you state in one sentence what the product does and who it's for, without using the words 'platform', 'AI', or 'solution'?
Why is this idea fundable in 2026 and not in 2018 or 2032? What changed that makes the window open now?
Who is the incumbent your customer pays today, even if it's a spreadsheet, an intern, or duct tape? Name them.
What measurable outcome does the customer get? (e.g., '8 hours/week saved per attorney', not 'increased efficiency')

regions.label: Customer
regions.intent: Get specific about who you're building for. 'Everyone' is not a customer. Names are customers.

questions.prompt: Can you list at least 10 named real people (first and last) who fit your buyer description?
What is the specific job title and seniority of the person who would write the check? Not 'enterprise', the actual role.
Is the person who uses the product the same person who pays for it? If not, who else has to say yes?
Can you name the first 10 customers by name AND describe how each one will hear about you, end-to-end?

regions.label: Evidence
regions.intent: What can you prove with real behavior — not statements of interest, not 'I'd definitely use that', but actual money or actual time spent?

questions.prompt: Has anyone paid you (in money) for this, even once?
How many real customer-discovery conversations have you done with people you didn't already know? (Friends and supporters don't count.)
What is the strongest piece of behavioral evidence you have — something a customer DID, not something they said?
Can you name the top 3 objections you've heard repeatedly from prospects who chose not to engage?

regions.label: Pricing
regions.intent: Pricing is fiction until someone has flinched, negotiated, or paid. Get out of the model and into the conversation.

questions.prompt: Have you named a specific dollar number to at least 3 real prospects and watched their reaction?
Do you know which budget line your purchase comes out of, and who controls it?
What's the dollar value of the outcome you produce for the customer? Show your math.
What is the customer paying today (in money OR time) to live with the problem? Be specific.

regions.label: Distribution
regions.intent: Most products that fail had better tech than the ones that won. Distribution is the product. Pick one channel and prove it.

questions.prompt: If you could only use ONE channel to reach customers, which would it be — and have you proven you can get even one customer through it?
What does it cost (in dollars or hours) to acquire one paying customer today? Show the actual math, not a model.
Who in your network can introduce you to your first 10 customers without you having to cold-pitch them?
If your CAC doubles tomorrow (it will), does this channel still work? What's the back-up?

regions.label: Team
regions.intent: Founder-team composition is the strongest predictor of which products get built well — and which never get sold.

questions.prompt: Which founder is going to make the next 20 sales calls personally?
What does this company need to do well in the next 18 months that nobody on the team has done before?
Name 3 people who would tell you the truth about your business if you asked, and when you last sat down with each.
How many months of personal runway do you have, and what's your plan when it runs out?
